summary: Leaves removed from Paris Manuscript B by Guglielmo Libri, sold to the Earl of Ashburnham as no. 2037, now Institut de France Ms. 2184.
history: sold to Bertram, 4th Earl of Ashburnham, 1847
sold by the 5th Earl to the Bibliotheque nationale, 1888

value.text: Formerly part of Manuscript B, now Institut Ms. 2184

claims.statement: Ashburnham 2037 is taken to be the leaves from Manuscript B, now Institut Ms. 2184. This pairing combines a listing that gives 2037 from B and 2038 from A with the Institut records that bind B with Ms. 2184 (facsimile of mss B 2173 and 2184) and A with Ms. 2185 (Manuscript A, Ms. 2172 and Ms. 2185).

claims.statement: Libri sold 1923 manuscripts, among them the Leonardo leaves, to Bertram, 4th Earl of Ashburnham, for 8000 pounds in March 1847; Libri was convicted in absentia by a French court in 1850.

sources.cite: Wikipedia, Bertram Ashburnham, 4th Earl of Ashburnham (background only).
